title: Replacing a Kitchen Sink: Removal, Fit, and Faucet Install (Ask This Old House)
summary: This Old House shows a step‑by‑step kitchen sink replacement, including turning off the water and disconnecting faucet supply lines, removing the old sink and its sealant from the countertop, adjusting a mis-sized opening with an oscillating saw, dropping in a standard replacement sink, mounting a new faucet with a base plate, applying silicone sealant, securing the sink with under-sink clips, and routing the drainage with an ABS-to-PVC adapter and a dishwasher tailpiece, followed by a final water test to confirm a leak-free install.
topics: Disconnect supply hoses (faucet) and shutoff valves
Disconnect sink drain and drain nuts
Remove sink from countertop clips and sealant
Protect laminate while removing sink (putty knife technique)
Adjust countertop opening with oscillating saw
Replace worn shutoff valves (washer and screw condition)
Faucet installation with base plate and bracket
Drain adaptation: two-inch ABS to 1-1/2-inch PVC with mechanical coupling
Final water test and leak check

sections.title: Prep and shutoffs
sections.description:
Turn off the water supply, verify lines, disconnect faucet supply hoses, and loosen the drain nuts to detach the drain.
Evidence: Turning the water off, disconnecting supply hoses, and draining actions are described in early transcript lines (00:11–00:32; 00:44–00:55).

sections.title: Remove old sink from countertop
sections.description: Loosen sink-to-countertop clips with a screwdriver, then pry the sink free with a putty knife to avoid damaging the laminate; prepare to remove the old unit (clip removal at 01:14; prying at 01:29–01:39).

sections.title: Fit new sink opening
sections.description: Drop in a standard 33 x 22-inch sink, test fit, notice the opening bows, and trim the opening with an oscillating saw to achieve proper clearance (opening measurements and saw use described 01:56–02:58).

sections.title: Shutoff valves inspection and replacement
sections.description: Inspect worn shutoff washers and a broken screw; decide to replace shutoff valves for reliability and easier future maintenance (03:10–03:41).

sections.title: Faucet installation and sealing
sections.description: Choose a four-hole faucet with a base plate; install from above the counter with a metal washer and brass bracket, tighten screws, and prepare a blank for a soap dispenser while applying a silicone bead around the edge to seal (04:09–05:28, including 05:07–05:16).

sections.title: Under-sink mounting and drain prep
sections.description: Secure the new sink with under-sink clips, trim the drain for the single-bowl setup, and prepare the drain area for final connections (05:28–06:24).

sections.title: Drain and water connections
sections.description: Adapt 2-inch ABS to 1-1/2 inch PVC with a mechanical coupling, connect the dishwasher discharge tailpiece, and assemble the water supply lines with flexible fittings (06:53–07:31).

sections.title: Final test
sections.description: Turn the water back on and confirm the installation is leak-free (07:31–07:35).
